You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The issue described is an infinite loop in HelpFormatter's wrapping code when a word is longer than the line width, causing the JVM to run out of memory and crash.

From the test and bug report, the failure occurs when printing help with a very narrow width (like 20), and a word in the description is longer than this width.

Inspecting the HelpFormatter.printHelp method shows it calls printWrapped to print header, footer, and long option descriptions line-wrapped.

The core wrapping logic is in HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer sb, int width, int nextLineTabStop, String text).

This method uses findWrapPos to find the position to wrap text at or returns -1 if no wrap needed.

The code splits the string at the wrap position and appends the first part plus a newline to sb, then continues processing the remainder of the text in a loop.

If pos == -1 (meaning no wrap needed), the entire text is appended and the loop returns.

However, the infinite loop occurs because findWrapPos returns wrap position as follows:

- It looks for newline or tab within width; if found returns its position+1.

- Otherwise, if the remaining string is shorter than width, returns -1.

- Otherwise tries to find the last whitespace character within width characters (starting at startPos+width, going backwards).

- If none found, tries to find the first whitespace character after startPos+width.

- Returns that position or -1 if none found.

The problem arises when there's a very long word longer than width with no whitespace at all. The backward search fails because no whitespace within width. The forward search tries to scan past the string end until whitespace found, but when none found, it returns -1.

In renderWrappedText, during the loop, text is re-assigned to "padding + text.substring(pos).trim();". If pos == -1, substring(pos) will be substring(-1), which in Java throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, so it can't be that. So pos must be >=0 here.

But inside the loop, the logic prevents infinite looping by checking if pos == nextLineTabStop - 1 when text length > width, then pos is forcibly set to width.

However, if the line consists solely of one very long word without spaces, pos might keep being the same value (e.g., 0 or nextLineTabStop - 1), causing text to never shrink and the loop to repeat endlessly appending.

Thus, the infinite loop is caused because when a word is longer than the width and no whitespace is found, findWrapPos returns a position that does not advance the substring effectively shrinking text in renderWrappedText, causing the while(true) loop to never terminate.

In the test case, the description "This description is Long." probably fits, but the bug report example "This is a looooong description" (very long word "looooong" fitting width poorly) triggers the infinite loop.

The root cause is that renderWrappedText lacks a robustness check for when the wrap position is close or equal to the nextLineTabStop - 1 and text length is more than width, making it adjust pos forcibly to width, but this is not sufficient when the wrapping position is very constrained resulting in no progress – the substring keeps the string the same, so infinite repetition.

Therefore, the infinite loop is caused by renderWrappedText interpreting the wrap position returned by findWrapPos incorrectly when the description contains a single long word with no whitespace, and it fails to properly advance to shorten the text in each iteration, causing the loop to never exit and memory to grow endlessly.

In summary, the infinite loop bug happens due to renderWrappedText not properly handling the case where the wrap position is at or near the start with no whitespace breaks and the line is longer than width, causing the loop to never shrink the string in the loop body.

Suggested fix areas: HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText and HelpFormatter.findWrapPos to properly handle long words wider than width, e.g., by wrapping within the word forcibly or detecting no progress and breaking the loop.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
